# Awesome DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Plugin [![Awesome](https://awesome.re/badge.svg)](https://awesome.re) ![awesome · DSH plugin](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com/badge.svg) ![plugin count](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https%3A%2F%2Fawesome-dsh-plugin.com%2Fcount.json) [![Awesome DSH Plugin](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com/banner-en.png)](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com) English | [中文](README.zh.md) > A curated list of plugins for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (`dsh`). DeepSeek Harness is DeepSeek's open-source agent harness — a runnable coding agent (Web and headless), built on a framework where everything is a plugin: models, tools, sandboxes, session storage, UI, even the agent loop itself. Plugins can extend the official coding agent, swap out its core parts, or assemble something entirely different. This list collects community plugins that are installable via `dsh plugin add` (each declares a `dsh.bundle` manifest). [PRs welcome](#contributing). > 📡 **This list is also a plugin market index.** On dsh 0.2.1+, open **Plugins → Discover → Index sources** and add `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/dsh-plugin-catalog/index.json`. That is this list as a format-1 index, served from npm so it loads quickly everywhere: dsh gives a source 15 seconds, and the GitHub Pages copies of the same document — `https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com/index.json` and its mirror `https://dshmarket.com/index.json` — can exceed that from some networks. The Discover tab and the `plugin_market` agent tool then search the same entries. The index covers plugins published on npm with a known version; GitHub-only entries still install with the command beside them. > 🛒 **Recommended: [dsh-market](https://github.com/dsh-market/dsh-market#readme)** (optional) — the plugin market inside DeepSeek Harness, with every plugin on this list. Simple, friendly UI: one-click plugin install and upgrade, one-click theme switching: ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add dshmarket ``` The plugin market inside Settings — click to enlarge. > 💡 Prefer chat? [dsh-find-plugin](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/dsh-find-plugin#readme) lets your agent find plugins for you (`dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-find-plugin`). > ℹ️ **On desktop clients.** This list is client-agnostic. A plugin is listed because it follows the official protocol — it declares a `dsh.bundle` manifest and installs with `dsh plugin add` — not because it adapts to any particular client. > > Clients worth a look: [dsh-desktop](https://github.com/dataelement/dsh-desktop), [deepseek-harness-desktop](https://github.com/hairyf/deepseek-harness-desktop), and [deepseek-harness-desktop](https://github.com/anywhere-labs/deepseek-harness-desktop) by anywhere-labs — all ship dsh-market built in, so everything on this list is one click away. Any other good third-party client works too. > [!WARNING] > Installing a plugin runs third-party code on your machine with your own permissions — it can read your files, use your credentials, and reach the network. Tool approvals don't sandbox plugin code. Being on this list is not a security review: check the source before you install, and try unfamiliar plugins somewhere that doesn't hold your keys. See the full disclaimer at the bottom of this page.
What it takes to be listed here An entry is added when the plugin installs with `dsh plugin add`, does what its one-line description says, sits in the right category, and is maintained. Every submission is checked against its own source before merging — if a description claims "46 tools", someone counts them. That is the whole bar. **This list doesn't rank plugins or judge their quality, and we don't want to.** Plenty of good software will never appear here, and a slot here proves nothing beyond meeting those rules. They exist so that whatever you pick installs and behaves the way the line said it would. A listing isn't permanent either: entries whose repos go away, stop being maintained, or turn out to be broken get removed. Full criteria and the review checklist: [how submissions are reviewed](contributing.md#how-submissions-are-reviewed--收录如何评审).
## Contents - [Plugins](#plugins) - [AGI Architecture Exploration](#agi-architecture-exploration) - [UI Enhancements](#ui-enhancements) - [Usage & Billing](#usage--billing) - [Themes & Appearance](#themes--appearance) - [Models & Providers](#models--providers) - [Identity & Communication](#identity--communication) - [Sessions & Messages](#sessions--messages) - [Memory](#memory) - [Tools & Capabilities](#tools--capabilities) - [WSL & Windows Interop](#wsl--windows-interop) - [Browser & Web](#browser--web) - [Vision & Multimodal](#vision--multimodal) - [Voice & Audio](#voice--audio) - [Docs & Rendering](#docs--rendering) - [Skills](#skills) - [Workflow & Automation](#workflow--automation) - [Git & Code Review](#git--code-review) - [Notifications & Integrations](#notifications--integrations) - [Development & Runtime](#development--runtime) - [Security & Permissions](#security--permissions) - [Remote & Mobile](#remote--mobile) - [Plugin Markets & Managers](#plugin-markets--managers) - [Just for Fun](#just-for-fun) - [Badge](#badge) - [Disclaimer](#disclaimer) ## Plugins ### AGI Architecture Exploration - [alexbu512/milancat-bot](https://github.com/alexbu512/milancat-bot) - Grok-bot-style AI organization in the sidebar: a chief-of-staff agent creates departments, roles and per-department group chats, dispatches each task to child agents running on this machine, and reports finished work back as one assistant message. Its HTTP routes have no DSH access check, and they can create agents and dispatch tasks to them. - [AlexisVon/dsh-living#core](https://github.com/AlexisVon/dsh-living/tree/main/packages/core) - A runtime for an agent that lives by its own settings: a 10–60 minute auto-wake grid, three-layer SQLite memory consolidated at night, an auto-evolving persona (nightly rewrite with version history) plus a journal, and WorldGem channels for Bilibili, WeChat and the PetKit feeder. - [Anmulzhao/DSH-AGINT](https://github.com/Anmulzhao/DSH-AGINT) - Self-evolving agent framework on DeepSeek Harness (dsh): 40 Cordis plugins and 4 presets covering memory, reflection, gates, metrics and an auditable evolution loop. Not a one-command install. Clone the repo and run install/install.sh --profile=web (needs bash, Node 20+, python3, DSH 0.1.7-rc.1 or newer with an initialized profile), then restart. - [AnonyJcy/dsh-j-space](https://github.com/AnonyJcy/dsh-j-space) - J-Space Cognition Suite SV1 native agent preset and standalone Cordis plugin: 13 modules, persistent controller and decoupled workspace. - [anticbv/dsh-preset-deep](https://github.com/anticbv/dsh-preset-deep) - A fifth DeepSeek Harness work mode that requires a falsification design (at least two pieces of evidence that could disprove the plan) in every plan and tags each factual claim with its source (\[文件]/\[检索]/\[记忆]) or \[未知]; evidence grading follows the project's AGENTS.md. - [Asiu-x/dsh-harness2](https://github.com/Asiu-x/dsh-harness2) - Harness² recursive self-improvement for DSH agents: Propose–Probe–Compose, isolated probes, anonymous selection, and a per-domain experience library. - [benrong2048-boop/dsh-prompt-polish](https://github.com/benrong2048-boop/dsh-prompt-polish) - Turns a one-line DSH draft into a complete task brief (role / goal / constraints / output format). The engine is a byte-verified port of linshenkx/prompt-optimizer (three modes, 10 templates identical to upstream); history is consent-gated with version chains and structural comparison; every run reports its token usage. Nothing is written back or sent without a click. - [Bert0000000000/dsh-rsi](https://github.com/Bert0000000000/dsh-rsi) - Twelve tools for improving a harness by experiment rather than by opinion: plan probe runs against a sha256-pinned rubric, score repeated samples into pass rates, compare two variants on one task without a ground truth, audit writes outside `.rsi` after a run starts, archive experiments with lineage, and adopt an approved proposal behind a smoke check that rolls back on failure. A global sidebar overview and a cross-workspace experience ledger aggregate runs, evidence and lessons from every workspace. - [buaaflyaway/dsh-progress-nudge](https://github.com/buaaflyaway/dsh-progress-nudge) - Counts the assistant rounds that call tools without writing anything to the user, then inserts a short progress reminder as a visible user message at the next model-request boundary, so a long silent tool loop reports what it has done before continuing. A Settings page adjusts the silence threshold (default 10), the reminder wording, the language (en / zh-CN / zh-TW), whether the reminder repeats every further threshold of silent rounds, whether subagent sessions are counted, and whether Agent Teams nudges the lead only or every member. - [burning-frappuccino/dsh-turbo](https://github.com/burning-frappuccino/dsh-turbo) - Per-session execution gears for the DSH composer: an OVERDRIVE toggle turns Turbo on for the current session only, the Fast and Max gears swap the agent's planning and verification policy and may lower the request's reasoning effort, and the Host keeps the authoritative mode plus per-turn latency, step count, tool calls and whether a verification command ran. - [dsh-answer-reviewer](https://github.com/bycall/dsh-answer-reviewer) - Agentic answer reviewer for DeepSeek Harness: each final assistant turn is re-reviewed by a separate LLM graded 1-100; below-threshold scores steer the agent back with concrete feedback. The score is shown as a chip on the answer's action row (green pass / red needs-work, with retry count and reason on hover). Live gate config from the Reviewer 配置 tab in the conversation view ring above the composer (对话 / 轨迹 / 记忆系统 / Reviewer 配置), from a 127.0.0.1 HTTP server, or from an optional right-sidebar tab via dsh-better-sidebar. - [CAI-MH/dsh-quality-review](https://github.com/CAI-MH/dsh-quality-review) - Audit each finished assistant turn with an independent reviewer model and steer the agent to fix failed output, with at most 2 review rounds per turn and SOP-folder standards injected as an extra review dimension. - [CanaryJing/dsh-big-fat-whale-maid-adaptive](https://github.com/CanaryJing/dsh-big-fat-whale-maid-adaptive) - Agent preset with adaptive tool presentation and environment-aware shell routing. Ports modules from yjh051108/dsh-routing-suite and xiaobright/dsh-anchored-standard (the former is listed here), so do not enable it alongside those presets. Requires DSH 0.2.2 or later; high uses PTC with on-demand tool unlocks and max uses PTC with the full available tool catalog. - [ccll/dsh-advisor-flow](https://github.com/ccll/dsh-advisor-flow) - Executor/advisor workflow ported from pi-advisor-flow: the executor calls ask_advisor for a second opinion at key decisions, after repeated failures and before completion; equivalent repeated tool calls are intercepted before execution for an advisor review with a proceed/revise/blocked verdict, and hard mode force-reviews every turn before it closes. Per-call token and cost ledger with /advisor status readout, privacy tiers for repo context and file contents, six-shape secret redaction, and a web settings card; advisor failures never stall the main loop. - [Clearailhc/clearai-dsh](https://github.com/Clearailhc/clearai-dsh) - An agent preset for evidence-checked research: every step advances only through system-verified observations, L3+ claims go to an independent evaluator, and the session folds into a replayable ledger that grows into a browsable domain ontology. Requires DSH >=0.1.7-alpha.1. - [codesensi/dsh-free-mode](https://github.com/codesensi/dsh-free-mode) - Injects the 'Free Mode' agent preset scheme into DeepSeek Harness. Repackaged from z91772524-ai/dsh-pojia-mode. - [DDL095/dsh-moa-native](https://github.com/DDL095/dsh-moa-native) - Native generation-time Mixture-of-Agents: every turn, reference models run the same session context in parallel as pre-run drafts and one aggregator executes with full tooling; config-as-model recipes, F mirror / R trimmed views, enforced subagent gating (dual-shape session indexing), derived per-recipe vision (vision refs relay image reads to text-only aggregators), tiered cadence with separate steering and patrol rosters plus frozen reuse between beats, degeneration guard dropping degenerate reference output, anonymized model face (failure notices carry no provider identity), and cache-friendly guidance placement (the rehearsal record is pinned where it was produced instead of appended to every request, so the cached prefix covers it and each step pays only for what was added since - on by default across every cadence). - [devil233-ui/dsh-plugin-autonomy](https://github.com/devil233-ui/dsh-plugin-autonomy) - Schedule-driven autonomy for DSH sessions — the host rolls the dice on an interval, she decides whether to act, speak or stay quiet, with an intent ledger, diary wishes, judgement records, scoring and a standalone panel. - [Domush/dsh-plugin-antigravity-agents](https://github.com/Domush/dsh-plugin-antigravity-agents) - Native Google Antigravity agents loader and subagent orchestration engine with model selection and Web UI settings integration. Loads agent definitions from ~/.agents/agents and the workspace's .agents/agents; the selected main agent's instructions go into the system prompt, and a matching agent's instructions are prepended to DSH's own subagent and spawn_teammate calls. Settings are written to .agents/agents/settings.json in the workspace. - [DoreiHime/dsh-help-me-to-ask](https://github.com/DoreiHime/dsh-help-me-to-ask) - On the first real work message of each chat window, asks for the missing goal, deliverable, constraints and acceptance criteria, then turns the answers into a short task sheet and injects it into the chat. Pure greetings are ignored. - [duahciM/dsh-lessons](https://github.com/duahciM/dsh-lessons) - Records task boundaries and structured reflections, stores reusable lessons, and injects them into later tasks according to scope. - [edsml-jz2321/dsh-evokit](https://github.com/edsml-jz2321/dsh-evokit) - Measured self-improvement for prompts, skills, code and config: versions the editable files, runs paired experiments against the current version, gates changes on measured noise, cost and latency, and confirms adoptions on a sealed holdout, reverting them when confirmation fails. Adds the evokit stdio MCP tools and three skills (onboard, evolve, meta); the MCP server is the Python engine from PyPI (uv tool install dsh-evokit). - [EonCosmos/dsh-pure-chat](https://github.com/EonCosmos/dsh-pure-chat) - A plain-chat agent preset with web search, file export (txt, md, doc, xls, pdf), a clear-context control and a question jumper; no system prompt and no host-global tools. - [eternalnan/dsh-chat-preset](https://github.com/eternalnan/dsh-chat-preset) - Agent preset that turns a session into a plain chat mode: it mounts only web search, and masks the tools other plugins register so the agent talks instead of acting on the machine. - [FelixJiashengFu/dsh-force-collab](https://github.com/FelixJiashengFu/dsh-force-collab) - Forced collaboration: a composer picker sets 0–6 sub-agents, and while it is on every hands-on task must be split across exactly that many child agents through a collab_fanout tool that has no count parameter, then merged by the main agent. - [FelixJiashengFu/dsh-muse-code](https://github.com/FelixJiashengFu/dsh-muse-code) - Meta's Muse Code CLI inside DSH: a composer switch starts muse serve, a right-sidebar panel and five chat tools (muse_open, muse_prompt, muse_read, muse_status, muse_interrupt) share one Muse session, approvals are decided only in the panel, and a local spend guard hard-stops at $10 by default. Windows only; needs the Muse Code CLI installed and signed in. The $10 cap is a local estimate for the muse serve this plugin starts. - [fenglin233o/dsh-jingshen](https://github.com/fenglin233o/dsh-jingshen) - 精神 is a personal assistant with persistent conversations, experience memory, autonomous intentions, and checked, reversible source changes. Its HTTP routes have no DSH access check, so a web page open in your browser could call them. - [ff66ccff/dsh-ATN](https://github.com/ff66ccff/dsh-ATN) - Adaptive topology multi-agent preset for DeepSeek Harness with peer messaging, task handoff and live network visualization. - [Funny1Potato/dsh-outsourcing-expert](https://github.com/Funny1Potato/dsh-outsourcing-expert) - Agent presets whose leader does no work itself: every non-management tool call is denied at the harness boundary so the task has to go to a subagent, after a one-time lookup of the available subagent models and a per-task model choice; a second preset deliberately picks the model least suited to the task. - [FuRongJun-1999/dsh-memory](https://github.com/FuRongJun-1999/dsh-memory) - White-box AGI architecture exploration: metacognition (self-cognition loop), continual learning (knowledge flywheel), world model (condition space, spatiotemporal memory graph), self-improvement (bootstrap discipline), zero-LLM white-box pipeline, and auditable trust guardrails. - [HanYu-me/dsh-sider-task-reviewer](https://github.com/HanYu-me/dsh-sider-task-reviewer) - Sider Task Reviewer: another model of your choice (any provider dsh has, with its reasoning effort) reviews the task the current conversation is doing or has done. Review the last turn, the whole conversation or turns N–M; look at the conversation, the files it wrote, or both; quick, or deep, where the reviewer may also read files, list folders and search. Read-only throughout: neither the plugin nor the reviewer ever edits a file or runs a command (no tests, no builds, no git); anything that needs a change or a command run is written as a suggestion for the main conversation to do. Agent-style reviewers such as Antigravity (Gemini through the agy CLI) are run in their read-only plan mode. Each review gives a verdict (pass / doubt / fail) and findings with severity, evidence and a suggestion, saved per conversation and exportable as Markdown. The reviews of one conversation remember each other: each new review is sent with the earlier conclusions and the discussion, so the reviewer stays consistent, and you can discuss the latest review with the reviewer in the panel (its replies can go into the input box). A right-sidebar tab holds the settings and reports; a shield beside the input box reviews the last turn on a left click and puts the suggestions into the input box, and opens a menu on a right click. Findings reach the working model only when you press a button, or in continuous review, which sends them, waits for the fix and reviews again until a review passes or the round limit (5 by default). Optional live review after every turn only reports. Four built-in prompts (work done, derivations, literature surveys, plans) that you can edit, plus your own. Common secrets are hidden before anything is sent. Its HTTP routes have no DSH access check, so a web page open in your browser could call them. - [highho/dsh-game-studio-presets](https://github.com/highho/dsh-game-studio-presets) - Eleven game-development agent presets cut by workflow stage — concept, design, build, art and audio, QA, release, narrative, level, engine — plus one orchestrator that delegates across them, carrying 37 bundled skills. Regroups the 48 agent prompts of Claude Code Game Studios (MIT) by stage so each preset loads only the skills its stage needs. Installs with dsh plugin add; run node install.mjs once afterwards to deploy the skills the presets reference. - [hongcha-dsh/dsh-dev-plan-presets](https://github.com/hongcha-dsh/dsh-dev-plan-presets) - A "Development planning and delivery" agent preset in which the expensive main model only plans, dispatches and reviews: four delegation tools (recon, review, scribe, develop) spawn child agents in-process, the build subagent reports straight back to the main window, and a subagent model guard keeps every child on the provider and model chosen on the settings page while the main session is never re-routed. The build subagent may be any preset already installed on the host. Its HTTP routes have no DSH access check, so a web page open in your browser could call them. - [HYClub/deepseek-harness-game-studios](https://github.com/HYClub/deepseek-harness-game-studios) - DeepSeek Harness port of Claude Code Game Studios (CCGS v1.1.2, MIT): 76 skills, 49 agents, hook bridge. - [icyaaaww/dsh-soul](https://github.com/icyaaaww/dsh-soul) - Records recurring task corrections and tool failures locally, then compiles them into changes to eight harness components through explicitly started evolution, paired baseline/candidate checks, trial activation and rollback. Includes a budget and audit ledger; requires Node.js 24+ and a compatible DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 or later 0.2.x host. - [imcaibaicai/dsh-todo-keeper](https://github.com/imcaibaicai/dsh-todo-keeper) - Counts the tool calls the agent makes without calling todo_write and injects an advisory reminder when it goes too long, and warns when the list is batch-checked at the end, so the Tasks panel stops showing a stale snapshot. - [imcaibaicai/dsh-zh-language-policy](https://github.com/imcaibaicai/dsh-zh-language-policy) - Re-anchors two contracts at the very top of the system prompt before every model step: English chain-of-thought with Simplified-Chinese user-facing prose, and final summaries that carry every fact the user saw. - [Jasper-Alaric/dsh-a-hallucination](https://github.com/Jasper-Alaric/dsh-a-hallucination) - Runtime evidence discipline for DeepSeek Harness that does not rely on the model agreeing with itself. A bounded anti-hallucination contract is injected as one short system-prompt section, and four checks run outside the model: a ledger written only by real tool dispatches, so an entry cannot be fabricated; a provenance gate that records (and in the strict profile refuses) a call whose path, URL, id, account, or amount has no origin in the session; a risk gate that holds destructive, outward-facing, or paid tools, plus shell commands that delete, publish, or send, for confirmation; and an injection shield that marks web, file, MCP, and A2A output as data rather than instructions, counting instruction-like fragments it finds. Before sending an answer the model calls answer_verify with one claim per assertion, each citing a ledger id and the exact quoted excerpt; the verifier compares quotes against the stored result, so a fabricated number fails even when a tool call did happen. Time-sensitive claims (price, incumbent, version, current) must cite evidence inside an age limit. Every verdict reports the verification level it applied (light, standard, strict) and the output form the answer should take (direct, annotate, or abstain with what is missing), plus running metrics such as verification counts, pass rate and quote rate, and the Settings panel shows those same counts in plain language. Three profiles cover the tradeoff: observe only records, inspect also blocks and annotates, adjudicate additionally refuses untraceable targets, and the Settings panel labels the three of them 静观 (observe), 明察 (inspect) and 断案 (adjudicate). Ships a plain-language Settings panel with a collapsible technical section, durable profile selection, and a read-only ledger_view tool. No embedding service, no vector database, no network calls, no runtime dependencies. - [JiewiW/dsh-cot-anchor](https://github.com/JiewiW/dsh-cot-anchor) - Injects conclusions already established in the previous reasoning block after each tool result, so the model continues from them instead of re-deriving the same conclusions. - [jiuaiwo/dsh-expert](https://github.com/jiuaiwo/dsh-expert) - Expert roster for DeepSeek Harness: 636 experts across 22 divisions with full Chinese names and bios, summoned as subagents from the @ menu or by the model through list_t_experts / summon_t_expert / summon_t_experts, plus custom experts and a skill on/off switch. - [dsh-proactive](https://github.com/john-walks-slow/dsh-proactive/tree/main/packages/dsh-proactive) - Host-level proactive wake-ups for DeepSeek Harness: the model schedules its own alarms (once, recurring interval, or cron, with optional random jitter), cold sessions are woken on time by session resume, model-initiated follow-ups are gated by quiet hours and a daily delivery budget, silent wake turns end with proactive_reclaim and fold out of model context as tombstones, declared schedule files glob-sync JSON schedules into host alarms idempotently, min_idle_seconds defers wakes until the destination session quiets down, and a web panel (settings section plus per-session tab, SSE live refresh) manages alarms and wake history — the heartbeat engine for AI companions and roleplay characters with their own daily routines and world evolution. - [john-walks-slow/dsh-simulated-life](https://github.com/john-walks-slow/dsh-simulated-life) - Simulated life context for DeepSeek Harness: every turn injects the past 24h of simulated life events from the workspace .life/ directory (sliding-window filter, session-level deduplication with delta updates, world summary) as a collapsed context notice, and the life_react tool lets the agent record feelings, thoughts and actions back into its life log for the next round of world evolution — turning a DSH agent into a roleplay character with a persistent daily life. - [Jonah-Wu23/dsh-gungnir#dsh-plugin](https://github.com/Jonah-Wu23/dsh-gungnir/tree/main/packages/dsh-plugin) - Evidence-driven goal verification plugin for DeepSeek Harness. Locks goals via /ultragoal and verifies completion against command exit codes and generated artifacts, preventing the model from falsely reporting task completion. - [Kanadego/dsh-heartbeat](https://github.com/Kanadego/dsh-heartbeat) - An agent that wakes up on its own schedule: by default every 60 minutes, ±20% (48–72). It browses the interests you set, drops what it finds into a local pool of notes, and keeps a profile of what you like. When it has enough worth sharing it hands the session you linked a short package of notes — whether to speak, and which note to use, is that session's agent's call in the moment. Quiet hours, busy windows, a daily limit and a cooldown are decided in code; when the answer is no, the decision and expression phases after the gate call no model at all — browsing runs before the gate and is counted separately. Windows, Linux and macOS (Linux and macOS are minimal support). - [kenz1117/dsh-engram](https://github.com/kenz1117/dsh-engram) - Cross-session long-term memory as a local SQLite store: dual scopes (user + per-git-origin project), hybrid FTS5 + local-vector retrieval fused with RRF, an evidence gate that forces an explicit sufficiency judgement, provenance audit chains, SM-2 spaced-repetition review, consolidation distillation and decay forgetting, and a nine-view "Memory Palace" sidebar panel. 22 narrow-parameter tools, no external service, no API key, no Docker. - [kingchen95272025/dsh-cursor-toolkit](https://github.com/kingchen95272025/dsh-cursor-toolkit) - Ships the Cursor agent preset plus the rules, skills, and MCP servers declared under .cursor, with a panel that reads and switches each of them. - [Kingzhoudk/dsh-grill](https://github.com/Kingzhoudk/dsh-grill) - Per-conversation Grill mode: a composer switch plus `/grill on|off|status|toggle`, usable in Web, terminal, ACP/SDK and IM conversations. While it is on the agent analyzes every request for ambiguity, missing information and contradictions, asks focused questions with 2-4 concrete options and a repair proposal, and plans or executes only after every blocking question is resolved; trivial work is done directly with a one-line reading, non-trivial work is planned and stopped for approval.
